deities: Lord Shiva (lingam with Nandi - one of the oldest temples of the fort; the Hidimba/Hidimbi legend is its namesake)

history.dynasty: Hoysala (12th-century inscription recorded on the temple); fort itself built in stages by Rashtrakutas, Kalyana Chalukyas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara and the Nayakas of Chitradurga, finished by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan
history.period: 12th century inscription (Hoysala era); among the oldest of the 18 temples of the upper fort
history.summary: One of the 18 temples in the upper fort of Chitradurga (Elusuttina Kote / Kallina Kote), on the hilltop reached by steps; described as the oldest and most interesting of the fort's temples. Mahabharata legend: the rakshasa Hidimba and his sister Hidimbi lived on this hill; during the Pandavas' exile Bhima fought and slew Hidimba and married Hidimbi - their son was Ghatotkacha; the boulders around are said to have been the arsenal in the duel. The temple displays the tooth of Hidimba, a large iron-plate cylinder (~3 m circumference, ~2 m high) called the Bheri or Drum of Bhima, a monolithic pillar and two swing frames at its gate. A 12th-century Hoysala inscription carved on the temple explicitly records this as the site of Bhima's marriage to Hidimbi (per a 2025 documentary travel report citing ASI examination - verify), which would predate the famous Hidimbi temple at Manali (c. 1500 AD). Note: one traveller report says the temple is 'built in stone but not used for worship any more' - active worship status unverified (verify).

name: Hidimbeshwar Temple
town: Inside Chitradurga Fort, Chitradurga (CSV town 'Chitradurga' correct)
town_description: The temple stands in the upper fort of Chitradurga (Elusuttina Kote - the fort of seven circular walls, also called Kallina Kote), on the rocky hill ~1 km from Chitradurga city, reached via the zigzag seven concentric fortifications and 19 gateways. The fort covers ~1500 acres and is famed for its rainwater-harvesting tanks and the Onake Obavva Kindi legend.

travel.airport: Hubli - about 186 km; Bengaluru (Kempegowda International) - about 197 km (both domestic/international options per travel guides).
travel.railway: Chitradurga railway station - buses and taxis available to the fort.
travel.road: Chitradurga city lies on NH-4/NH-48, ~200 km from Bengaluru (3-4 hrs by KSRTC bus incl. Airavat coaches); autos/taxis from Chitradurga bus stand to the fort.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Fort open 10:00 AM-5:30 PM daily (verify); entry fee reported INR 20 (e-ticket)/25 (cash) for Indian/SAARC/BIMSTEC visitors and INR 250/300 for other foreign nationals, free for children below 15 (verify); no separate entry fee for the temple.
